The [Arts Quad](/wiki/Arts_Quad "Arts Quad") on Cornell's main campus with [McGraw Tower](/wiki/McGraw_Tower "McGraw Tower") and Olin and [Uris](/wiki/Uris_Library "Uris Library") libraries in the background

Cornell University's main campus is located in [Ithaca, New York](/wiki/Ithaca,_New_York "Ithaca, New York"), on East Hill, offering views of the city and [Cayuga Lake](/wiki/Cayuga_Lake "Cayuga Lake"). The campus has expanded to approximately 745 acres (301 ha) since its founding, now including multiple academic buildings, laboratories, administrative facilities, athletic centers, auditoriums, museums, and residential areas.[[44]](#cite_note-45)[[45]](#cite_note-ithaca-46) In 2011, *[Travel + Leisure](/wiki/Travel_%2B_Leisure "Travel + Leisure")* recognized Cornell's campus in Ithaca as one of the most beautiful in the United States, praising its unique blend of architectural styles, historic landmarks, and picturesque surroundings.[[46]](#cite_note-47)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/34/Cornell_University%2C_Ho_Plaza_and_Sage_Hall.jpg/250px-Cornell_University%2C_Ho_Plaza_and_Sage_Hall.jpg)](/wiki/File:Cornell_University,_Ho_Plaza_and_Sage_Hall.jpg)

Ho Plaza seen from McGraw Tower with [Sage Hall](/wiki/Sage_Hall "Sage Hall") and [Barnes Hall](/wiki/Barnes_Hall "Barnes Hall") in the background

The Ithaca campus is characterized by an irregular layout and a mix of architectural styles that developed over time through successive master plans. More ornate buildings generally predate [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), while later construction reflects [modernist](/wiki/Modern_architecture "Modern architecture") and contemporary styles.[[47]](#cite_note-48)

Cuban Missile Crisis :: Aftermath :: Human casualties :: chunk_0042
The body of U-2 pilot Anderson was returned to the US and was buried with full military honours in [South Carolina](/wiki/South_Carolina "South Carolina"). He was the first recipient of the newly created [Air Force Cross](/wiki/Air_Force_Cross_(United_States) "Air Force Cross (United States)"), which was awarded posthumously. Although Anderson was the only combatant fatality during the crisis, 11 crew members of three reconnaissance Boeing [RB-47 Stratojets](/wiki/RB-47_Stratojet "RB-47 Stratojet") of the 55th Strategic Reconnaissance Wing were also killed in crashes during the period between 27 September and 11 November 1962.[[214]](#cite_note-216) Seven crew died when a [Military Air Transport Service](/wiki/Military_Air_Transport_Service "Military Air Transport Service") Boeing [C-135B Stratolifter](/wiki/Boeing_C-135_Stratolifter "Boeing C-135 Stratolifter") delivering ammunition to Guantanamo Bay Naval Base stalled and crashed on landing approach on 23 October.[[215]](#cite_note-217)

Blackpink :: Career :: 2010–2016: Formation and pre-debut activities :: part 01 :: chunk_0002
Blackpink began forming in 2010 when [YG Entertainment](/wiki/YG_Entertainment "YG Entertainment") held tryouts worldwide for preteen or teenage recruits to create a new girl group after launching its first major one, [2NE1](/wiki/2NE1 "2NE1"), the previous year. According to the members, joining the label as [trainees](/wiki/Korean_idol#Trainee_system "Korean idol") was akin to enrolling in a full-time pop-star academy, with [Jennie](/wiki/Jennie_(singer) "Jennie (singer)") describing the experience as "more strict than school" and [Rosé](/wiki/Ros%C3%A9_(singer) "Rosé (singer)") comparing it to *[The X Factor](/wiki/The_X_Factor "The X Factor")* with dorm rooms. For members who had left their lives outside of South Korea, the pace of training alongside the culture shock was especially difficult.[[3]](#cite_note-bbcover-3) Preparations for Blackpink's debut began as early as 2011, when YG Entertainment revealed on November 14 that their new girl group would debut in the early half of 2012 and feature at least seven members.[[4]](#cite_note-4) Consequently, numerous news stories and rumors surfaced surrounding the new girl group's debut being delayed, although there had been no official information.[[5]](#cite_note-5) It was until May 18, 2016, that YG Entertainment confirmed the girl group would debut that July, stating that the members were selected through years of stiff competition.[[6]](#cite_note-6) The label later confirmed that Jang Hanna and [Moon Sua](/wiki/Moon_Sua "Moon Sua"), who were introduced to the public as potential members of the new girl group, were not included in the lineup.[[7]](#cite_note-7)[[8]](#cite_note-8)

Jennie, the group's main rapper and lead vocalist, was the first member revealed on June 1, 2016.[[9]](#cite_note-9)[[10]](#cite_note-roles-10) She joined YG Entertainment as a trainee in 2010 after moving back to South Korea from New Zealand

Wright brothers :: Flights :: Gliders :: 1900 :: chunk_0008
[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/WrightBrothers1900Glider.jpg/250px-WrightBrothers1900Glider.jpg)](/wiki/File:WrightBrothers1900Glider.jpg)

The 1900 glider. No photo was taken with a pilot aboard.

The brothers flew the glider for only a few days in early autumn 1900 at Kitty Hawk. In the first tests, probably on October 3, Wilbur was aboard while the glider flew as a kite not far above the ground with men below holding tether ropes.[[52]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrouch2003188–189-53) Most of the kite tests were unpiloted, with sandbags or chains and even a local boy as ballast.[[53]](#cite_note-54)

They tested wing-warping using control ropes from the ground. The glider was also tested unmanned while suspended from a small homemade tower. Wilbur, but not Orville, made about a dozen free glides on only a single day, October 20. For those tests the brothers trekked four miles (6 km) south to the [Kill Devil Hills](/wiki/Kill_Devil_Hills "Kill Devil Hills"), a group of sand dunes up to 100 feet (30 m) high (where they made camp in each of the next three years). Although the glider's lift was less than expected, the brothers were encouraged because the craft's front elevator worked well and they had no accidents. However, the small number of free glides meant they were not able to give wing-warping a true test.

The pilot lay flat on the lower wing, as planned, to reduce aerodynamic drag. As a glide ended, the pilot was supposed to lower himself to a vertical position through an opening in the wing and land on his feet with his arms wrapped over the framework. Within a few glides, however, they discovered the pilot could remain prone on the wing, headfirst, without undue danger when landing. They made all their flights in that position for the next five years.

Logo of YouTube Kids

[YouTube Kids](/wiki/YouTube_Kids "YouTube Kids") is an American children's video app developed by YouTube, a subsidiary of [Google](/wiki/Google "Google"). The app was developed in response to parental and government scrutiny on the content available to children. The app provides a version of the service oriented towards children, with curated selections of content, parental control features, and filtering of videos deemed inappropriate viewing for children aged under 13, 8 or 5, depending on the age grouping chosen. First released on February 15, 2015, as an [Android](/wiki/Android_(operating_system) "Android (operating system)") and [iOS](/wiki/IOS "IOS") [mobile app](/wiki/Mobile_app "Mobile app"), the app has since been released for [LG](/wiki/LG_Electronics "LG Electronics"), [Samsung](/wiki/Samsung_Electronics "Samsung Electronics"), and [Sony](/wiki/Sony "Sony") [smart TVs](/wiki/Smart_TV "Smart TV"), as well as for [Android TV](/wiki/Android_TV "Android TV"). On May 27, 2020, it became available on [Apple TV](/wiki/Apple_TV_(device) "Apple TV (device)"). As of September 2019, the app is available in 69 countries, including Hong Kong and Macau, and one province. YouTube launched a web-based version of YouTube Kids on August 30, 2019.[[187]](#cite_note-187)
